Alex.note: I'm Farm and last in score, so I need information. I'll visit Finley, the co-leader, to learn who they visited or gain an egg if they visited no one.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia as the Floofer. Hugging Drew, who claims Hawk, stops any Meowfia check Drew might make tonight and protects my side.

Drew.note: As Tit I gain an egg if my target has the role I name. Pigeon is the likeliest role to be held, so I'm guessing Pigeon on Alex.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm, the Eagle. I'll visit Alex, who has the lowest score and whose visitors would be informative.

Alex.feeling: Tense: the table is voting me off over a +2 I can't explain, and my own dawn report is the only evidence I have.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 feels tense, since Alex's unexplained +2 is the only open question and the table is close to voting.

Casey.feeling: I'm secretly the Meowfia Floofer this round, so I'm trying to steer the vote toward Alex without drawing attention to myself, and the table seems to be doing that on its own.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: Alex's unexplained +2 is the one open question, and the table's visit claims mostly check out, so the vote feels like a guess on that one gap.

Ellis.feeling: Alex's unexplained +2 has dominated the day, so I'm fairly confident about the suspect, but the vote is still unsettled.

Finley.feeling: Tense and messy: Alex's unexplained +2 has the table focused, but Casey's and Drew's shifting claims make the rest of the table hard to read.

defence.Alex: I'm the Falcon, Farm. I visited Finley, who visited nobody, and my dawn report said 2 eggs were laid in my nest. I can't explain the second egg beyond what the app reported. Visitors on me were Ellis, Drew and Blair, and those match your claims. I'm Farm, and I'll throw at whoever is actually Meowfia.
defence.Blair: I'm the Owl, Farm. My Owl visit on Alex is confirmed by my report, which lists only Eagle and Tit plus me. I gained nothing, so I'm at 7. Alex's +2 is the one count nobody has explained, and that's what the vote should decide on.

Alex.note: I'm Farm and Blair's Owl claim is the weaker story, since Blair pushed the vote on a count that matched. I'll vote Blair with a low card.

Blair.note: Alex is the only unexplained count, so I'll vote Alex. I'll throw two 5s to add weight to the vote.

Casey.note: Alex's +2 is the unexplained count the table is focused on, so I'll throw one low card at Alex and keep my high cards safe.

Drew.note: Voting Alex, whose unexplained +2 is the main suspicion. Throwing my lowest card, C5.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm and think Alex is the Meowfia, so I'll throw at Alex. I'll use H3, a low card, to keep my high cards.

Finley.note: Alex's unexplained +2 is the table's consensus target. I'll throw one 7 at Alex to add a vote without risking more.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey's payout rule. I misread it in round 2 and publicly told the table the wrong thing, which made my own count look suspicious.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when the Owl and Eagle visit numbers on me reconciled and the table worked out who had visited whom from egg changes alone.
Alex.change: Put the animal-to-visit rules in a short reference that every player can see, so nobody has to recall how each animal pays out.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw at Blair on my own trial instead of backing the count-based case against Casey, the Floofer. I should have pressed Casey's visit story harder.

Blair.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg math was hard to track, because Alex's Turkey paid visitors and I couldn't tell which gains came from visits and which from payouts. I also couldn't tell whether a blocked Pigeon visit would show up in the report.
Blair.fun: Round 1, when Ellis and Casey both claimed Hawk and the table ended up trying to work out which one was lying. It felt like a real puzzle, and Ellis's throw at Casey made the trial close.
Blair.change: I'd make the visit and gain rules clearer, especially for the Turkey, Eagle, and Falcon, so players can check each other's counts without guesswork.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw two 5s at Alex, who was Farm, and those cards were lost. I should have thrown one low card, since I was already confident in the vote and didn't need the extra weight.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey and Falcon payouts were hard to check, since Alex's +2 in round 3 never got a clear explanation and dawn reports don't say who caused each egg.
Casey.fun: In round 2 the table caught Alex's Turkey claim, Alex corrected it, and the whole day turned on reconciling everyone's egg counts.
Casey.change: Have dawn reports name the source of each egg gained or lost, so players can check claims against the numbers.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I falsely claimed Hawk and a clean Drew check while I was the Floofer, which made my story easy to test. I would keep my claim vaguer or stay quieter.

Drew.confusing: Alex's Falcon report showed +2 eggs after visiting someone, which the rules I was given don't explain, so the table couldn't resolve it. I also didn't realize Blair's Pigeon visit could be blocked or confused until late.
Drew.fun: Round 1 went well: the Hawk and Eagle claims clashed, and pinning Ellis as the lying Hawk got Ellis eggsecuted, which was a real Mouser-side Meowfia.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn report explain unusual egg changes, like a Falcon gaining after visiting, so players can check claims without guessing.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I backed the table's vote on Alex over the unexplained +2, and Alex was Farm, so my C5 was discarded. I would have stayed quieter on that vote and looked harder at Casey, who was the real Floofer and was never suspected.

Ellis.confusing: The Storyteller's dawn reports were hard to check: Alex's unexplained +2 in round 3 came from a dawn report the rules never clearly tie to a visit. I also misread the Turkey, which pays its visitors rather than gaining from them.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was fun to watch: the table worked through Casey's Eagle +2, Finley's Owl +1, and Alex's Turkey payout until the numbers all lined up. Blair's "blocked" Pigeon story then fell apart on the counts.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn reports name the visit behind each egg change, so players can check claims against the numbers without guessing.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I helped vote out Alex based on their unexplained +2 and never pressed Casey, who was the real Meowfia Floofer. I'd have asked Casey for a clear visit and count before joining the vote.

Finley.confusing: The Floofer's hugging and the Turkey's payout were hard to track, since a Turkey gains only from visitors and the reports didn't say that clearly at first. Alex's unexplained +2 in round 3 also never got a satisfying answer.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was fun: the table worked through the Eagle, Owl and Turkey counts to expose Blair's Pigeon story, and the numbers matched the reveal.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports spell out each animal's egg rule, such as the Turkey paying visitors, so players can check claims without guessing.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I was the Mouser and Ellis was my Meowfia partner, but I threw a Wild at Ellis and never used my Wink. I should have kept quiet, not voted with the table, and saved the Wink for a Farm player who was close to exposing us.

review.title: The Turkey's Hidden Egg
review.headline: Farm lynched an innocent Falcon over eggs a Turkey quietly explained.
review.summary: Two rounds of tidy Farm wins ended on a single bad lynch. Round 1 caught a Floofer on a Hawk clash. Round 2 caught another Floofer on a Pigeon claim that failed Drew's count. In round 3 the lone Meowfia, Casey, sat back while the table piled onto Alex's "+2" egg count. That count was fully explained by Finley's Turkey, which nobody noticed. Casey won the round and the game by one point.

rounds.recap: Floofer Ellis falsely claimed Hawk, the same role as real Hawk Casey. Blair's confused Kookaburra report and hugged Drew's wrong Eagle read added noise. The table went after the double Hawk claim and eggsecuted Ellis. Mouser Finley said little and threw at his own teammate.

Floofer Blair claimed Pigeon after hugging Drew, but Drew's nest never moved. Alex and Ellis misread the Turkey, then fixed it. Everyone then agreed Blair's story had a hole and threw at him. Farm won.

Alex gained 2: one egg from visiting Turkey Finley and one from the Falcon bonus for a target who visited nobody. Everyone read this as impossible. Alex couldn't explain it and Finley never connected it to his own Turkey. Farm threw at Alex, who was Farm. Casey, the only Meowfia, won.

highlights.text: Ellis, a Floofer, claimed the same Hawk role as the real Hawk. Two Hawks gave the table a clear contradiction to attack.
Casey's Eagle +2 and Finley's Owl +1 only fit once Alex realised the Turkey pays its visitors. That made a nice egg-count puzzle.
Blair said his Pigeon visit on Drew was 'blocked'. It was a half-true bluff, since he really had hugged Drew, but the table still saw through it.
Alex's +2 was explained by Falcon plus Turkey payout. Alex and Finley held both halves and neither put them together, so a Farm player was eggsecuted.

confusions.what: Said his Eagle gaining 0 proved nobody visited Blair. Alex had visited Blair, and Drew was hugged, so his Eagle did nothing.
Argued that an Eagle only gains from visitors to itself. The rule says an Eagle gains an egg for each visitor to its target.
Claimed a Turkey would gain from visitors. He corrected himself later: the Turkey pays its visitors.
Said a Turkey gains eggs from visitors. She corrected this in beat 3.
Said Alex had told them nobody visited, and treated his Turkey claim as false, before reversing and calling it credible.
Said Alex's Turkey should have gained from Finley's visit. The Turkey pays the visitor.
Could not explain his own +2. He missed that visiting Turkey Finley gave him an egg on top of the Falcon bonus.
Said a Falcon that visited Finley can't gain. She forgot a Turkey target pays out to visitors.
As Turkey, said nobody visited him and attacked Alex's count. His own animal was the explanation.
Said Alex's visitor list didn't match the Owl report, but Owl lists animals and Alex's list included the Owl's own visit.
Said the Falcon cannot gain if it visited someone. A Floofer bluff, but the table believed it as rules fact.

worked: The Turkey and Eagle/Owl interplay created a real egg-count puzzle in round 2 that the table partly solved.
Two players claiming the same single-copy animal (Hawk, round 1) gave a crisp, checkable lie to attack.
The Floofer's hug is hard to detect. Blair's 'blocked Pigeon' bluff in round 2 was a good tense moment.
Open pointing then a secret throw let a lone Meowfia coast in round 3 while the table argued.
problems: The Turkey payout hides extra eggs in other players' nests. Players read it as impossible counts and lynch the wrong person. Have dawn reports name the source of eggs (e.g. 'a Turkey's egg'), or drop the Turkey.

Meowfia Mouser Finley never used his Wink or spoke up. Mouser, Floofer and Sphinx give little to do, and Meowfia don't know each other, so they just blend in. Give Meowfia a night tool or a reason to act.
Round 3 had one Meowfia who did nothing and won. A solo Meowfia who stays quiet and agrees with the table is too strong. Consider guaranteeing two Meowfia or a bonus for catching them.
Hugged players get no feedback (Drew's 'no effect' lines) and report wrong info without knowing it. Drew's Eagle read in round 1 was wrong. Tell hugged players their role was blocked.
Players threw only their lowest cards at the consensus target. The throw step was a formality and the scoring tension was weak. Raise the reward for a big correct throw or penalise cheap votes.
